**GreenLight Fund Brings One Degree to Charlotte to Open Access to Millions of Dollars Worth of Benefits and Resources**


**CHARLOTTE, NC – November 16, 2026** – Today, GreenLight Fund Charlotte announced a multi-year investment in[One Degree](https://greenlightfund.org/organization/one-degree/charlotte/) , a nonprofit organization started in California, to address the complex and fragmented social services ecosystem. One Degree is actively building partnerships and a digital public infrastructure with collaborators across Charlotte-Mecklenburg. Beginning in early 2027, One Degree aims to reach 30,000 Charlotte residents and connect 100 local organizations to over $2,250,000 worth of resources over the next four years.


One Degree is a 501(c)(3) technology-driven nonprofit committed to helping low-income individuals and families access the resources they need to achieve social and economic mobility and improve their lives through a comprehensive online resource guide. By partnering with government, healthcare, and community-based organizations, One Degree is designed to bridge the gap between low-income communities and vital resources, empowering people to build healthy, fulfilling lives.


**Sam Smith, Jr., Executive Director of[GreenLight Fund Charlotte](https://greenlightfund.org/sites/charlotte/) ,** shared, “At GreenLight Fund Charlotte, we believe that every individual and family deserves access to the resources and opportunities they need to thrive. Yet, too often, families in our community face barriers not because support doesn’t exist, but because navigating available resources can be overwhelming and complex. One Degree brings an innovative, proven approach to bridging that gap by connecting individuals and families to critical services and benefits that can strengthen their financial stability and overall well-being. We are excited to welcome One Degree to Charlotte and work alongside community partners to ensure more residents can access the support they need to build a more stable and prosperous future.”


One Degree is launching its work in Charlotte with Crisis Assistance Ministry as its first implementing partner and is actively seeking opportunities to collaborate with additional community, civic, and other organizations serving families. Through this initial partnership, One Degree will strengthen coordination and collaboration across Crisis Assistance Ministry’s network of agencies, improving closed-loop referrals and access to critical resources for individuals and families experiencing financial crises. As One Degree expands its partnerships throughout the community, it aims to create a more connected and coordinated system of support that helps individuals and families achieve greater financial stability and long-term self-sufficiency.


**Carol Hardison, Chief Executive Officer of Crisis Assistance Ministry,** states, “Crisis Assistance Ministry provides families with housing stability support after a financial crisis, but many need additional services to stay on steady ground. One Degree’s arrival in Charlotte gives our neighbors a new, accessible way to find those resources, and it strengthens the network of support that makes our whole community more resilient.”


After a year-long selection effort with GreenLight Charlotte’s Selection Advisory Council, we identified financial resiliency and benefit navigation as immediate opportunities. GreenLight’s investment in One Degree comes at a critical time, as the need to bridge the gap between communities facing systemic economic barriers and vital resources continues to grow. Roughly 38% of Mecklenburg County households live below the local cost-of-living threshold, yet eligible Charlotte residents leave tens of millions of dollars in vital public benefits unclaimed every year. This disconnect stems from outdated systems and a lack of digital infrastructure that create significant barriers for individuals and families seeking help. One Degree’s innovative software and digital networks are designed to seamlessly connect communities disproportionately impacted by economic inequities with vital, life-affirming care.


**Rey Faustino, CEO & Founder, One Degree** noted, “What we heard from organizations in Charlotte is clear: the services are here, but families are still falling through the gaps between them. One Degree exists to close those gaps. We’re coming to Charlotte to strengthen what already exists, building the connective infrastructure that helps local organizations work together and makes it easier for families to get the support they need.”


One Degree’s cloud-powered technology solutions platform provides free online tools that help individuals and families find local services and public benefits, resulting in a holistic, supportive path to social and economic mobility. The One Degree Community Platform lets users search for, save, and track community resources based on their needs. One Degree also helps nonprofit professionals find and share opportunities with clients. One Degree’s goal is to make identifying and accessing community resources easier while complementing the work nonprofits and government agencies are already doing.


GreenLight Charlotte’s multi-year financial and on-the-ground strategic support, along with strong local partnerships, positions One Degree to achieve impact in both the short and long term. Additional financial investments from public and private partnerships will ensure program sustainability for years to come. Full rollout of One Degree is underway with plans to reach 5,000 individuals in 2027 while continuing to expand to other community-based organizations in Charlotte.


One Degree is the fifth organization GreenLight Charlotte has invested in bringing to Charlotte, joining[Inner Explorer](https://greenlightfund.org/organization/inner-explorer/charlotte/) ,[Center for Employment Opportunities](https://greenlightfund.org/organization/center-for-employment-opportunities/charlotte/) ,[ParentChild+](https://greenlightfund.org/organization/parentchild/charlotte/) and[Alternatives to Violence](https://greenlightfund.org/organization/alternatives-to-violence/charlotte/) .
